# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - This week continued to be dominated by the Eurozone, whether by ongoing policy debate, which seemed to gain some kind of focus in the past week, or by fresh downgrades of European banks. The return of the Chinese to the market saw physical premiums on the Shanghai Gold Ecxhange tighten noticeably at the beginning of the week and then fade a little in gold as the price rallied through the week. The ongoing recovery in prices has met resistance in gold around $1,684-1,690 and in palladium we see the price making a move back towards $634-636 as part of a correctional recovery from the $550 level seen in the previous week. • The most recent Commitment of Traders Report reveals that gold, silver and palladium enjoyed a recovery in investor interest as recent very sharp declines proved unsustainable. Only platinum continued to see a decline in NYMEX positioning on the price rebound. • Gold saw a recovery in ETF interest as continued fears over the Eurozone inclined investors towards thinking that gold will outperform industrial metals over the medium term. Silver was neutral with a negligible decline in ETF length. Both platinum and palladium saw continued reductions in ETF length as investors continued to take a battering from recent price falls. ###### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **17 October 2011** ###### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ###### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ###### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ###### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ###### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **17 October 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 11 October 2011; ETF data to 14 October 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**||||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**|| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| ||_Futures_||_Options_||**COMEX Total**|||||| |**Date**|**Large Specs**

The return of the Chinese sector after the Golden week holiday was a boost, with anecdotal evidence of very decent jewellery demand over the Chinese holiday, and with Gold trading at a $20 per Troy Ounce premium on the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE) on Monday the 10th. As the price rose through the week however, physical demand started to cool, quickly responding to higher prices. The rally was partly a natural correction to the oversold conditions of the previous fortnight, of course, when the 9 day Relative Strength Index dropped to 22.70, levels not seen since August and mid-September of 2008. Later in the week, renewed concern over capital adequacy in the European banking sector and more downgrades for UK and French banks helped promote a gold-positive environment. ##### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—October 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Net long speculative positions in gold on COMEX rose for the first time since early September, rising by 777,000 ounces. Given the 11 million ounce drop since mid August, taking positioning down to the lowest level since July 2009, a switch to buying seems reasonable. The charge was led by the small spec category, with only small spec option positioning declining. TOCOM liquidated slightly, perhaps helped by the weakening JPY offering more attractive prices to longs. - Buying interest returned in the ETF sector, however it remained mixed, with the Swiss being the notable buyers but some selling seen elsewhere. Total ETF length now comes in at 67.30 million ounces. 2

- Silver started the week at $31.34 basis December futures, and essentially had a strong week aided by the recovery in gold, and a steady copper price (trading at over $7,525 per tonne mid-week) with decent speculative length added within COMEX. There was some evidence that recent upside call selling (versus put buying) was being reversed on the dip in prices and this would have given another small boost to prices as dealers bought back hedges. With Diwali approaching in late October, physical demand for silver remains healthy. Technically, silver needs to break and close above the $32.80 level and ideally the $36.80 level in order to really shake off the downtrend seen since early September. - Net silver speculative longs on COMEX rose by just over 10 million Troy ounces in the week to October 11th. Given the collapse in speculative length to levels not seen since late 2008, it was not really surprising to see buying interest return, as mentioned in last week’s edition of this report, as such significant destruction in speculative length reflected a healthy, albeit painful correction in positioning. - ETF positions were scarcely changed this week. Generally ETF investors have ignored t

he sharp falls in price recently, preferring to add to their positions during the drop. This week they trod water in what remains a tough market to call. Total holdings are 465.5 million ounces. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **17 October 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 11 October 2011; ETF data to 14 October 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Platinum opened the week at $1,493 basis Jan futures and scarcely looked back as the Chinese returned to the market after Golden week and the premium on the SGE widened to $65 on Monday the 10th. There was an appreciation that although the outlook was gloomy, car unit sales were still steady. Combined with the dip below production costs in US$ terms and 9 day RSI dropping to around 15 (very over-sold looking), a rebound of some sort ought to have been on the cards. The only black mark was the impression that decent auto-sector buying on the big dip would probably cannibalise future demand and remove a significant element of demand if the price were to fall back again. - Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX fell again, this time by 68,000 ounces to 1.10 million ounces in the week to the 11th of October, their fifth successive weekly decline. It looks as if some short positions were added during the price recovery, judging by the increase in open interest versus the decline in net

length, suggesting that some investors are willing to bet against the durability of this recovery. TOCOM investors remained sellers for another week in succession, with long positions falling by 22,000 ounces to 264,000 ounces, a much slower pace than the decline of the previous three weeks, which averaged about 51,000 ounces of ‘reduction’ each week. - Platinum ETF holdings declined for the fifth successive week leading to the 14th of October. They now stand at 1.474 million ounces. The principal source of selling was from the ETFS (UK) fund. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **17 October 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 11 October 2011; ETF data to 14 October 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

Good auto buying helped the price off very oversold-looking levels. $600-603 is now acting as a support level, and the market ended the week on a very firm note, suggesting that the $634-636 target as part of the corrective bounce is very close to being achieved. Any further moves higher will encounter resistance at $650 and $695, just below the break-down level of the 21st-22nd September. As with platinum, a note of caution comes from the impression that demand from the auto sector was bought forward on the impressive dip to just below $550. - Investor longs in palladium staged a good recovery last week as about 95,000 ounces of length was added to NYMEX speculative positions. We are still at around 47 % of the length seen at the beginning of September however, so the context is one of a tremendous recent reduction in investor confidence. - The ETF sector saw further substantial redemptions in the week to October 14th. US ETFS investors seem particularly battered this past week. As usual, it seems the Swiss ETFs remain the most stubborn holders of metal.
